GPT-x, LLaMa, every other new model today Prior BERT: ELMoELMo(Peters et al., 2018; NAACL 2018 best paper)–Train two separate unidirectional LMs (left-to-right and right-to-left) based on LSTMs–Feature-based approach: pre-trained representations used as input to task-specific models–Trained on single sentences from 1B word benchmark (Chelbaet al., 2014) Train separate left-to-right and right-to-left LMs Apply as “Pre-trained Embeddings”

BERT: Key ContributionsA deep Transformer encoder model pre-trained on large corporaThe key: learning representations based on bidirectional contextWhy? Because both left and right contexts are important to understand the meaning of words.Example #1: we went to the river bank.Example #2: I need to go to bankto make a deposit.Pre-training objectives:

(1) masked language modeling + (2) next sentence prediction,State-of-the-art performance (2018) on a large set of sentence-level and token-level tasks. Masked Language Modelling (MLM)All input tokens participate in bidirectional self-attention BUT only the 15% of tokens sampled for prediction contribute to the training loss.Average cross-entropy loss over these selected positions Network weights are updated based on average CE loss over the sampled tokens Masked Language Modelling ExamplesHe is from Kuala Lumpur, Malaysia.àHe [MASK]from Kuala [MASK], Malaysia.He went to the store. àHe went to the [MASK].
MLM: Masking Rate and StrategyQ: What is the value of k?–They always use k = 15%.–Too little masking: computationally expensive–Too much masking: not enough context
How are masked tokens selected?–15% tokens are uniformly sampled–Is it optimal? See span masking (Joshi et al., 2020) –Example: He [MASK]from Kuala [MASK], Malaysia.

MLM: 80-10-10 CorruptionFor the 15% of tokens selected for prediction,–80% of the time, they replace it with [MASK] tokenwent to the storeàwent to the [MASK]–10% of the time, they replace it with a random word in the vocabularywent to the storeàwent to the running–10% of the time, they keep it unchangedwent to the storeàwent to the storeWhy? Because [MASK] tokens are never seen during fine-tuning Next Sentence Prediction (NSP)Motivation: many NLP downstream tasks require understanding the relationship between two sentences (e.g. NLI, paraphrase detection, QA)NSPis designed to reduce the gap between pre-training and fine-tuning Input = [CLS] the man went to [MASK] store [SEP] he bought a gallon [MASK] milk [SEP]Label = IsNextInput = [CLS] the man [MASK] to the store [SEP]penguin [MASK] are flight ##less birds [SEP]Label = NotNext [CLS]: a special token always at the beginning[CLS]: a special token used to separate two segments Next Sentence Prediction (NSP)

BERT pre-training: Putting togetherVocabulary size: 30,000 word pieces (common sub-word units) (Wu et al., 2016) Final input representation = Token + Segment + Position embeddings Separate two segments

BERT-base: 12 layers, 768 hidden size, 12 attention heads, 100M parametersBERT-large: 24 layers, 1024 hidden size, 16 attention heads, 340M parameters Training corpus: Wikipedia (2.5B) + BooksCorpus (0.8B)Max sequence size: 512 word piecesTrained for 1M steps, batch size 128k Same as OpenAI GPT OpenAI GPT was trained on BooksCorpus only! SummaryBERT is a deep bidirectional Transformer encoder pre-trained using masked language modelling.Bidirectional self-attention allows each token to attend to both its left and right context.BERT popularisedthe large-scale pretrain–then-fine-tune paradigm in NLP.Achieved state-of-the-art performance (2018) across diverse NLU tasks.
